## LLM Recipe

### 1.1 Data Curation &amp; Tokenization

#### [Language-Specific Effects of Tokenizer Choice in Multilingual Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12144>)

A controlled multilingual study measures how tokenizer choices affect individual languages and tests inexpensive metrics for screening candidates before model training. The results favor language-specific evaluation over a single average and show why allocating more tokenizer capacity to a low-resource language should be validated rather than assumed beneficial.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-11T10:02:36Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Tokenization, Multilingual, Controlled Ablations

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12144>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/cmeister/tokenizer-lm-ablations>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 2–6 compare 123 models spanning 54 tokenizers; the main setup uses 1.27B models and 9.2B tokens. Family-held-out ranking reaches 89.0% accuracy for mean FLORES+ bits-per-byte. Newly discovered October 8 paper, announced in October 9's batch; the linked artifact predates this analysis, so no earliest-public timestamp or new-weight release is asserted.

**Limitations:** Mostly one seed per tokenizer, one main architecture/vocabulary scale and observational metric correlations. Fixed tokens change training bytes; task-level generalization remains limited. GitHub and artifact history were inaccessible, and exact artifact parity is unverified.

### 1.7 Reinforcement Learning &amp; Reasoning

#### [When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12161>)

ZCPO folds length-normalized, group-centered policy divergence into frozen response-level update coefficients instead of adding a separate KL penalty. This makes reference-policy guidance interact with the same update controls as reward feedback, improving the tested reasoning and long-context training runs.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-11T10:02:36Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** RLVR, KL Regularization, Policy Optimization

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12161>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Table 1 reports Qwen2.5-32B AIME24/25 avg@32 of 56.8/48.5 versus 47.3/37.1 for DAPO without KL, averaged across three seeds and aligned by cumulative GPU compute. Newly discovered: October 9 00:00 UTC public availability is inferred from the dated NEW batch and official schedule.

**Limitations:** The proof optimizes coefficients for fixed inputs, not policy convergence; several mechanisms remain hypotheses. Full-vocabulary KL needs numerical care. The paper says runnable supplementary code exists, but no public implementation was verified. Results were not reproduced.

### 1.8 Distillation &amp; Model Compression

#### [Stochastic Teacher Intervention for Agentic On-Policy Distillation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10878>)

STI-OPD uses teacher–student disagreement to probabilistically replace a proposed agent turn before execution, then importance-weights supervision on teacher-generated tokens. This offers a training recipe for limiting compounding trajectory errors while leaving the student to act alone at evaluation time.

**Published:** 2026-10-07 · **First seen:** 2026-10-10T10:12:31Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** On-Policy Distillation, Teacher Intervention, Agent Training

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10878>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–4 and Table 2 report ScienceWorld success of 27.5% versus FutureBridge-OPD's 22.2% for a Qwen3-1.7B student and 4B teacher, alongside component ablations. Newly discovered: the October 7 receipt preceded its inferred October 9 00:00 UTC public announcement; an October 10 discovery checkpoint is retained.

**Limitations:** Importance weighting corrects teacher-token sampling at fixed contexts, not intervention-induced histories or adaptive selection. Teacher probabilities are required. Evidence uses small text-only Qwen students; matched intervention counts are not matched teacher FLOPs. No author code was verified.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.1 Agent Architecture &amp; Planning

#### [Plan-and-Patch: Diffusion Language Models for Agentic Planning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10786>)

Plan-and-Patch trains a diffusion model to generate structured agent plans and replace selected spans while preserving the surrounding steps. This makes local plan revision explicit and reduces planner-generation latency in two tested environments, while showing that finding the right repair region remains a bottleneck.

**Published:** 2026-10-07 · **First seen:** 2026-10-10T10:09:23Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Agent Planning, Diffusion Models, Plan Repair

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10786>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery from the October 9 NEW batch, item 7; v1 received October 7 at 18:45:45 UTC. Appendix A.2 reports generation latency of 14.3 versus 23.3 seconds on ALFWorld and 21.7 versus 40.2 seconds on TextCraft, with diffusion versus autoregressive 8B planners and a common Qwen3-8B executor.

**Limitations:** Latency is synchronized, unbatched bf16 planner decoding on one A100, excluding environment execution. Interactive success does not consistently favor diffusion; repair restarts from the initial state. One fine-tuning seed and different pretrained model families limit attribution. No author implementation was verified; results were not reproduced.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.4 Attention, KV Cache &amp; Memory Systems

#### [PageWeaver: KV-Guided Query Unions for Sparse Attention](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11201>)

PageWeaver groups sparse-attention queries by overlap in their selected KV pages, then executes them through a kernel that retains each query's original support and output location. This reduces repeated page traversal while accounting for the cost of constructing useful query groups.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-09T10:07:33Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Sparse Attention, KV Reuse, GPU Scheduling

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11201>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. On selected MiniMax-M3 H200 captures, online regrouping lowers complete-call latency by 3.26–7.66% versus original-order Union8, including preparation. Newly discovered: reviewed and deferred October 9; its inferred public release precedes this daily window.

**Limitations:** Incremental service throughput gains are only 0.47–0.73% at 32K/64K and negative at 8K. Few independent prompts, one generated token and no downstream quality evaluation; no win over the faster existing B300 backend. A dedicated public artifact URL was not verified.

### 3.5 Kernels, Compilers &amp; Runtimes

#### [SGLang and Miles on NVIDIA Vera Rubin](<https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-10-09-vera-rubin>)

SGLang retunes attention, communication and hybrid-model kernels for Rubin, while Miles connects rollout and training to CPU-hosted agent sandboxes. The report shows how removing memory, synchronization and launch overhead can improve a ported LLM stack, with small-scale RL runs checking the integrated execution path.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-11T10:04:14Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** SGLang, Kernel Fusion, Vera Rubin, RL Infrastructure

[Blog](<https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-10-09-vera-rubin>) · [Code](<https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang>) · [Project](<https://github.com/radixark/miles>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. For Kimi K3 NVFP4 on eight Rubin GPUs, fusing the MoE tail reportedly removes 276 launches per decode step and improves end-to-end performance by 5.9%. A separate MLA configuration improves 16% at batch 16/context 128K. Newly discovered October 9 report, recovered through the homepage after the blog index returned a shell.

**Limitations:** Configuration-specific gains are not additive. Early-access hardware; RL training reward is not held-out accuracy, and the FP8 DeepSeek test uses only four layers. The public Miles integration PR predates this report; the article does not establish first availability of every kernel patch.
